issues.description: The problem statement specifies a SealSaloon constructor that accepts a String (SealSaloon(String)) and implies storing an identifying name, but the provided solution implements a no-argument constructor (public SealSaloon()) and does not define a name field. The template's Main (commented example usage) also constructs SealSaloon with no arguments (new SealSaloon()). This mismatch between the specification and the actual code/usage is likely to confuse students about which constructor to implement and whether a name field is required, and may lead to compilation/runtime mismatches if students follow the problem text strictly.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the specification and the code: either update the problem statement/UML to require a no-argument constructor (SealSaloon()) or update the template and solution to include a constructor SealSaloon(String) and store the saloon name (and provide a getter). Alternatively, provide both constructors (SealSaloon() and SealSaloon(String)) so the example Main and the specification are both satisfied; document the expected constructor(s) clearly in the problem statement.
